_meta.scope: San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara
_meta.note: General safety-planning structure, NOT legal advice; review with a local DV advocate before launch. Themes follow the National DV Hotline safety-planning guide (https://www.thehotline.org/plan-for-safety/), which was not independently fetched.
_meta.how_to_use: Each step has home_actions (quiet things that can be done while the partner is nearby) and away_actions (things that need privacy). The app resolves resource_filters against resources.json using the user's county, urgency, constraints and channels (see match.py).
_meta.device_caution: Quiet channels can still leave traces (browser history, message threads, notifications, shared accounts). Prefer a safer device (library, work, friend) and delete threads where safe. Text 911 is a last resort when you cannot speak.

phases.title: I need to be safe now

steps.title: If you are in danger
home_actions: Text 911 if you cannot speak (call if you can).

steps.title: Reach an advocate
home_actions: Chat or text: National DV Hotline (chat at thehotline.org, text START to 88788); La Casa de las Madres text line (SF); SafeChat Silicon Valley (Santa Clara).
away_actions: Call a 24-hour hotline; ask for shelter, safety planning and transportation help.

steps.title: Emergency shelter
home_actions: Not usually possible quietly; save the hotline number to reach when you can speak.
away_actions: Call the 24-hour line. Shelter locations are confidential. Tell them if you have children or pets, and ask about eligibility.

steps.title: Pets
away_actions: San Mateo County: ask CORA about the Safe Pets Program (up to 30 days, free, CORA referral). SF and Santa Clara: no verified program found; ask the advocate.

steps.title: Getting there safely
away_actions: Ask the advocate or shelter intake about transportation. No published, verified ride program found in these counties yet.

steps.title: Make a plan with an advocate
home_actions: Chat/text an advocate; read the hotline's safety-planning guide on a safer device.
away_actions: Call a hotline; consider a Family Justice Center visit (Santa Clara: AACI FJC Thursdays; Sunnyvale FJC; San Mateo FJC status unconfirmed).

steps.title: Secure your phone and accounts
home_actions: Read NNEDV Safety Net guidance on a safer device; do not change settings that would alert the partner.
away_actions: Change passwords and review location sharing from a device the partner has never accessed.

steps.title: Keep your new address confidential
home_actions: Read about California Safe at Home.

steps.title: Gather documents and essentials
home_actions: Make a list in your head or on a safer device.
away_actions: Collect ID, immigration papers, medications, cash, keys; store copies with someone you trust or ask an advocate what is safe to take.

steps.title: Get on shelter and housing waitlists early
away_actions: SF: coordinated-entry access points for survivors (Asian Women's Shelter by phone; SafeHouse and Riley Center in person).

steps.title: Restraining order (DVRO)
home_actions: San Mateo: Family Law Facilitator LiveChat and Guide and File online forms. Santa Clara: court live chat/email via scscourt.org.
away_actions: Call or visit court self-help or legal aid (SF: CROC, Open Door Legal, JDC, Bay Area Legal Aid; Santa Clara: Restraining Order Help Center, Pro Bono Project; San Mateo: Bay Area Legal Aid).

steps.title: Custody and visitation
away_actions: Ask legal aid; Family Justice Center attorneys in Santa Clara (AACI, Thursdays).

steps.title: If immigration status is a worry
home_actions: Read provider pages; no call needed.
away_actions: Call a provider that lists VAWA / U-visa help (e.g., Bay Area Legal Aid San Mateo for DV survivors; CARECEN SF; Catholic Charities; CLSEPA; Immigration Services of Mountain View; AACI FJC). Several shelters state no citizenship requirement; confirm when you call.

steps.title: Court support and victim services
home_actions: San Francisco: submit the Mayor's Office for Victims' Rights online form and say when it is safe to call.
away_actions: San Mateo Victim Services (650-599-7479, open to all regardless of immigration status); Santa Clara Victim Services Unit.

steps.title: Apply to CalVCB
home_actions: Start the online application; no police report needed. Keep paperwork where it will not be found.
away_actions: Call 1-800-777-9229 or ask an advocate to help apply.
